correctness.rationale: Complementation is a bijection between perfect matchings and two-factors in each cubic prism. Matching classification separates matched-rung cases encoded by cardinality matchings of the base cycle from exactly two exceptional opposite-phase perfect matchings when n is even; complement component counts are proved for each case. The explicit binomial coefficient identity follows from a cyclic gap argument. The first Newton inequality for F_n(z)/z is contradicted by positive factorizations of its exact defect for every n>=8; all n=3..7 are proved real-rooted from displayed low-degree factors. A standalone direct perfect-matching complement enumeration confirms every coefficient for 3<=n<=14. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof of infinity.

value.rationale: Exact 2-factor component spectra in a canonical cubic planar vertex-transitive family refine old total/Hamiltonian counts and give a sharp all-order root-geometry boundary. The comparison with real-rooted cycle matching polynomials is structurally motivated, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The main value is the exact n=7/8 transition proved for every larger graph, not routine total-count recomputation.
